name: Reporting the Total Hours Each Employee Worked (Case 1)
description:
Suppose we have an input file that contains information about how many hours each employee of a company has worked. The file looks like the following (Employee's name, Hours):
Erica 7.5 8.5 10.25 8 8.5
Erin 10.5 11.5 12 11 10.75
Simone 8 8 8
...
Construct a program that reads this file and calculates the total number of hours worked by each individual. Make sure that the program handles each specific exception that could occur.

comments.content:
We need to first declare the function that receives a full path for a file that contains information about how many hours each employee of a company has worked, reads this file, and calculates the total number of hours worked by each individual. The given full file path is referred by variable file_name.

Note that all statements following the header line are indented.
The try blocks tries to execute the code within it. The statements in the try block may throw several types of exception.
If an error is encountered, the try block code execution is stopped and transferred down to the except block(s).
The open function opens the file. The variable file_name specifies the path to this file. We want to read the file; therefore, we open it in the read mode "r".
We could also call the open function without specifying the mode, because when only the filename is passed, the open function opens the file in read mode.
For reading lines from a file, we can loop over the file object.
This for loop assigns the name line to each of the lines in the file in turn, from the beginning of the file to the end, and then the statement in the loop body will be executed for each line.
Note that all statements inside the loop need to be indented with respect to the loop header.
We need to split the line into words and store the words in a list.

We use split() function with no arguments because we want the split function to separate strings using space character. Note that, by default, this function considers any number of whitespace characters as a word boundary.
tokens[0] gives us the element at index 0 of the list that represents the employee's name.
We need variable total to maintain a running total, which means the sum of the hours the employee worked. Of course, the total should be initialized with 0.

We use a for loop to iterate over the hours reported for the employee. We can get the hours that the employee has worked by accessing the second through the last element in the list of line tokens. We need the indexes to start at 1 with every integer number up to but not including the list length. We get this sequence by calling the range(1,len(tokens)) function.

Note that the loop starts at 1 because the value at the index 0 of the list is the employee's name. The hours the employee has worked start from the second element in the list of line tokens. Also, note that the function len(tokens) returns the number of the values in the list of line tokens.
Note that all statements inside the loop need to be indented with respect to the loop header.
If an error is encountered during calculating the total hours the employee has worked, the try block code execution is stopped and transferred down to the except block(s).

We need to add each reported hour to the running total that is stored in variable total. So, in each iteration, we add the reported hour to the variable total and store the result into the variable total.

We get the reported hour by accessing the element at index i of the list of line tokens. We need to covert this value to a float by calling the float function.

Note that we could perform the float conversion and addition in the same line. Also, note that each value that is stored in the list of line tokens is a string. Therefore, we need to convert the hours employee has worked into a number. We convert each hour to a number by calling the float() function because the reported hours could have a decimal point.

The += operator adds the reported hour to the value of the variable total and the result is stored in the variable total. Thus, this statement is equivalent to the statement total = total + float(tokens[i]).
We need to handle the ValueError. This error occurs when an hour that is reported for the employee is not a number and we call the function float() to convert that value to a float.
The body of this except block gets executed only if a reported hour in the line is not a number. Otherwise, the body of this except statement is skipped.
This statement prints to the default standard output stream the error that caused the ValueError. The printed text is followed by the end-of-line character at the end.

This statement concatenates the content of the given strings, variable name and total to print the total hours each employee has worked. We concatenate the content of these variables using the + operator. Variable name has a string value and we can use the + operator to concatenate its content with other strings. Variable total, on the other hand, has a float value and its value can be concatenated with strings only when it is explicitly converted to a string using the str function.
Note that the concatenating and printing are done in the same line. That is, we don't have to store the concatenated string to a new variable at first and then print it in the next line.
Note that the + operator creates a new string from the contents of its operands joined. This string will be printed by the print function and followed by the end-of-line character at the end.
We're done with reading the file; therefore, we use close() to close it and free up any system resources taken up by the open file.
We need to handle the FileNotFoundError. This error occurs when the file could not be found.
The body of this except block gets executed only if the file could not be found. Otherwise, the body of this except statement is skipped.
This statement prints to the default standard output stream the error that caused the FileNotFoundError. The printed text is followed by the end-of-line character at the end.
We need to handle the IOError. This error occurs when an error occurs when trying to read/close the file.
The body of this except block gets executed only if an error occurs when trying to read/close the file. Otherwise, the body of this except statement is skipped.
This statement prints to the default standard output stream the error that caused the IOError. The printed text is followed by the end-of-line character at the end.

We need to read the full file path that the user enters. To do this, we need to use the input() function. This statement prompts the user to enter the full path for a file, then reads the text entered by the user and places it in the variable name. The value that will be stored in variable name is a string.
This statement calls the report_work_hours function and passes the name as its arguments. Note that the function call must be done after the function is declared.
